practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Retains data-derived rule/prediction reasoning by explicitly selecting guide-listed linear regression; does not assess simulation construction.
practice_questions.solution: Use temperature as a predictor and sea level as the continuous response, fit a slope/intercept to paired observations, and use the fitted relation to estimate sea level for a specified temperature. Check fit against observed values before trusting predictions.

marking_points.criterion: Fits a linear relation/slope and intercept from paired data.

practice_questions.question_text: Evaluate testing a trained ML flood-warning model only on examples used during training, compared with using held-out representative cases.
practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Retains validation-with-known-results reasoning through explicit ML dataset splitting/evaluation,not general simulation testing.
practice_questions.solution: Training-only scores can be optimistic because the model may fit those particular examples. Held-out cases test prediction on unseen data and better reveal overfitting. They should represent relevant conditions and include difficult cases; a small or unrepresentative test set still gives uncertain evidence. Prefer a separate representative test set, review appropriate performance measures and investigate errors before deployment.

practice_questions.solution: RAM holds currently used geometry, textures and intermediate working results so the processor/GPU can access them during rendering.

practice_questions.question_text: Discuss processing-time and memory considerations when a live 3D display adds many more objects and higher-resolution textures.
practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Rebuilt scenario and response wording while retaining the supported reasoning; source-specific obsolete material excluded.
practice_questions.solution: More objects/pixels increase rendering work and can reduce frame rate unless processing throughput increases. A GPU can perform many similar graphics operations in parallel. Larger textures and working results need more RAM; insufficient capacity may force extra transfers or reduced detail. Choose processing and memory together against the target frame rate and acceptable detail, cost and power use.

marking_points.criterion: More graphics work increases time/reduces frame rate.
